title: Prone Positioning to Improve Survival in Severe ARDS Supported with ECMO – A Randomised Controlled Multi-Centre Trial
summary: The study investigates whether the chances of survival for patients with severe lung failure can be improved if they are positioned on their stomachs shortly after the start of ECMO therapy.

interventions.name: Patients assigned to the intervention arm will be placed in the prone position for 16 consecutive hours or longer every day. PP will be applied for a minimum of four consecutive sessions on four consecutive days after randomisation, and PP can then be continued at the discretion of the treating phys
Patients assigned to the control arm will remain in the supine position. PP is not permitted at any time in the control arm after initiation of ECMO up to EOS at day 90.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients with ARDS, as defined by the Berlin criteria
2. Male or female patients aged 18 years without upper age limit 
3. Reversible cause of ARDS, as determined by the treating physician(s) prior to VV ECMO cannulation
4. Severe ARDS refractory to conventional therapy placed on VV ECMO support within the preceding ≤ 24h
5. Written informed consent (obtained as described in CTP)
Exclusion criteria:
1. Initiation of VV ECMO > 24h
2. Any mechanical ventilation due to acute respiratory failure for more than 10 days before VV ECMO
3. Invasive mechanical ventilation due to acute respiratory failure for more than 7 days before VV ECMO
4. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation > 10 minutes before VV ECMO
5. End-stage chronic lung disease
6. Contraindications for prone positioning (e.g., but not exclusively, intracranial pressure > 30 mmHg or cerebral perfusion pressure < 60 mmHg; massive haemoptysis requiring an immediate surgical or interventional radiology procedure; tracheal surgery (excluding tracheostomy) or sternotomy during the previous 15 days; serious facial trauma or facial surgery during the previous 15 days; unstable spine, femur, or pelvic fractures; late stage of pregnancy, if prone positioning is anatomically no longer feasible or considered to endanger the wellbeing of the child or the mother) 
7. Patient moribund on the day of randomisation, SAPS II > 90
8. Liver cirrhosis (Child-Pugh Class B or C)
9. Lung transplantation
10. Burns on more than 20% of the body surface 
11. A diagnosis of COVID-19 as the most likely cause for the severity of respiratory failure, or positive COVID-19 testing within the previous 72 hours before randomisation
12. Simultaneous participation in other interventional trials which could interfere with this trial; simultaneous participation in registry and diagnostic trials is allowed
